scope: Source-asset review only; no runtime replacement or game acceptance.
authorship: Built-in imagegen redraw using the left-facing canonical and three right-facing video pose references. Preparation and recovery are newly drawn; these six poses are not six extracted original-video frames.

realMotionReferences.interpretation: Already airborne / torso relatively upright and legs hanging. Does not establish the actual takeoff moment.
Forward-leaning tucked airborne posture; cape lifts behind. Apex timing requires original trajectory.
Low landing posture; original platform contacts may conceal parts of feet.

anatomicalConstraints.facing: Left in all poses; no mirroring of the right-facing video
anatomicalConstraints.nearSide: Anatomical right arm/hand is near, grips fork on screen left
anatomicalConstraints.farSide: Anatomical left arm is far and may be occluded; left-hip lantern stays on far posterior hip at screen right partly behind cape
anatomicalConstraints.tether: Same near-shoulder brass ring connects via red tether to the fork; not exchanged between hands
anatomicalConstraints.referenceUse: Canonical defines proportions, short cape and equipment identity. Video defines gesture and motion phase; its small pixels do not establish fingers or exact near/far leg anatomy.
anatomicalConstraints.observed: No obvious extra limb or hand-to-leg fusion in this six-pose sheet; frame 4 cape spread and frame 6 return to original idle remain artistic review items.

scaleMeasurements.coordinates: Original 1536x1024 pixels; measurements are analysis only, no corrective scaling applied.

helmet.method: Manually selected upper/middle helmet cross-sections about 60px below crown. Measure warm helmet pixels with alpha>=128, R>100,G>75,B>40,R>1.04G,G>1.04B inside explicit x ranges. This is a comparable chord, not the physical full helmet diameter.

fork.method: Within manually selected fork-cup ROIs, measure alpha>=128 bone highlights (R>190,G>140,B>90). Select the two largest components not touching ROI edges, which isolate the two bone prongs, and measure maximum point distance over their union to reduce in-plane rotation effects.

scaleMeasurements.conclusion: Both markers remain in roughly the same scale range; pose 3 is larger in both measurements. Approximately 4% marker variation remains, with perspective, threshold and manual landmark uncertainty. This does not certify rigid-size consistency or justify per-frame bbox normalization.

layout.method: Explicit nonuniform source rects recover the pose-2 foot and pose-4 cape beyond nominal 512px grid lines. Each crop is placed at original cell-relative coordinates plus 64px margin.

registrationProposal.footMethod: Near-foot contact estimates use manually identified anatomical foot ROIs, alpha>=128, bottom-most 3px of that foot and median x. No whole-sprite bounding box was used.
registrationProposal.unresolved: After proposed pelvis x alignment, the near-foot contact x changes by about 115px from pose5 to pose6. Aligning the foot instead shifts the inferred pelvis by a comparable amount. Near/far occlusion and hand-marked hip uncertainty need checking, but uniform translation alone cannot satisfy both landmarks.
registrationProposal.decision: Do not apply a misleading final registration. Keep original crops, root:null and the explicit suggested offsets as review evidence. A dedicated foot/hip correction is required before gameplay acceptance.
registrationProposal.constraintCaution: A fixed pelvis is a diagnostic alignment candidate, not necessarily the correct landing solution. Actual support foot, body advance and weight transfer must be considered with both feet.
registrationProposal.nextCorrection: Redraw or reference-ground the pose5 to pose6 body motion and relative two-foot placement together; translation alone is not acceptance.

targetSizes.note: ai512 is model inference size, not 512px source detail. Keep native video crop and actual generated resolution separate.
targetSizes.currentDirections: V2 optimized left/right WebP files derive from corresponding canonical images. Current Godot still loads one legacy hero set and flips x; it does not load the canonical left sprite.
